reference.title: Scenario 3 — Paragraph before the first heading
reference.shortdesc: Consider a document where Normal paragraphs appear between the Title-styled paragraph and the first Heading

section.p: Consider a document where Normal paragraphs appear between the Title-styled paragraph and the first Heading 1 — for example, a version statement or an executive summary that appears after the document title.

row.entry: [Title]: Cloud Platform Guide [Normal]: Version 3.2 | April 2025 [Normal]: This guide covers installation, configuration, and administration. [Heading 1]: Installation

entry.codeblock:
... Cloud Platform Guide

Version 3.2 | April 2025

This guide covers installation, configuration, and administration.

section.p:
Result:Paragraphs placed between the Title and the first Heading 1 are treated as body content belonging to the title. The converter creates a DITA topic file using the document title as the topic title and places all paragraphs inside its as

elements.
section.note: Do not place important Normal paragraphs before the Title style. Pre-title content such as version numbers, draft status, confidentiality notices, or disclaimers may be excluded from the DITA output. If this content must appear in the converted DITA, apply a registered structural style, such as Disclaimer, Copyright, Notice, or another converter-supported style.
